title: Session log record
description:
One line of session.jsonl, written by `user-agent`.

Read the property list and note what is absent: there is no `severity`, no `pass`, no `status`, no `verdict`, no `issue`, no `recommendation`. This is the enforcement described in DESIGN.md section 1. The user-agent cannot certify that the app works, because there is nowhere in this schema to write a certification, and `additionalProperties: false` means inventing a field fails validation rather than being ignored.

`pqa validate` additionally reports a named error when a record carries a verdict-shaped key, because 'property "severity" is not allowed here' is a less useful message than an explanation of why.

step.description: Monotonic within a run. Referenced by `evidence_refs` in findings.

target.description: What was acted on, as the persona would name it ('the blue Save button'), not as the DOM names it.

expected.description: What the persona expected BEFORE acting. Required on every step: committing to an expectation in advance is a small guard against writing the expectation to fit the outcome.

observed.description: What appeared on screen. Description, not interpretation: 'the list is empty', not 'the data failed to load'.

felt.description: The persona's reaction, in the persona's words. This field is the raw material for `user_voice` in a finding, so its register matters more than its accuracy.

artifacts.description: Paths relative to the run directory, e.g. 'screenshots/step-004.png'.

oneOf.title: intent
oneOf.description: The first half of a two-phase step: what the persona is about to do and what they expect, written BEFORE acting. Optional -- a step is either one `observation`, or an `intent` followed by an `outcome` with the same step number. When used, the gate checks the ordering mechanically: an intent written after its outcome is an expectation fitted to the result, which is the thing the `expected` field exists to prevent.

expected.description: What the persona expects to happen. Committed before the outcome exists.

oneOf.title: outcome
oneOf.description: The second half of a two-phase step. Has no `expected` field on purpose: the expectation was committed in the intent record and cannot be restated once the result is known.

oneOf.title: perturbation
oneOf.description: Written by the persona-drift-check hook, not by the agent, when a sealed scenario perturbation falls due. The gate checks that every due perturbation has exactly one of these, that it matches what was sealed, and that it landed before the next step.

step.description: The last recorded step when the perturbation was injected. Equal to at_step unless the hook fired late.

oneOf.title: persona_injection
oneOf.description: Written by the persona-drift-check hook, not by the agent. Its presence at the expected cadence is checked by `pqa drift`.

oneOf.title: blocked
oneOf.description: Repeated interaction with no observable state change. DESIGN.md section 3: an agent stuck in a loop has usually found the defect, so this is recorded rather than silently retried.

oneOf.title: terminated
oneOf.description: The last record in a well-formed session log. `reason` is checked against run.json by the review gate.
